source.title: Beyond Output Matching: Preserving Internal Geometry in NVFP4 LLM Distillation
source.authors: Fang Tu; Jun-Hua Zhao; Chi Liu; Xin Chen; Hai-Feng Wu; Jian-Min Wan; Srinivasan Manoharan

record.tranche_reason: The study measures teacher–student representational similarity during NVFP4 quantization and distillation, and shows that the measured alignment changes substantially with the training objective. It does not test convergence among independently trained models or convergence with scale.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the reported CKA measurements and the text-described layerwise CKA trends. Benchmark accuracy and training efficiency results are not separate rows because they do not measure representational convergence.
record.test_reason: The study compares NVFP4-quantized students with their own frozen BF16 teacher, which is the same model with the same architecture, weights origin and data. It does not compare independently trained models. CKA serves as a diagnostic and as a training loss for the authors' CKA-QAD method, and the CKA-QAD rows show alignment produced on purpose by that loss. No result bears on whether independently trained models converge, whether convergence is partial or plateaus, or what causes it. The PTQ and KL-only drift finding is a related but different construct (teacher–student fidelity under compression), so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors also stress that the drift is most pronounced in RL-post-trained models. They frame CKA–accuracy as a correlation, not a guarantee.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies linear CKA as a training regularizer for NVFP4 quantization-aware distillation; it does not reproduce a method for testing convergence among independently trained models.
record.method_sensitivity: Measured CKA differs across PTQ, KL-only QAD, and CKA-QAD, and across layers; KL-only drift is particularly pronounced in specified Nemotron layers and at the final layer.

fits_no_version.finding: KL-only quantization-aware distillation lowers CKA to the BF16 teacher below the PTQ level, despite recovering accuracy. Nemotron: avg 0.993 to 0.958, last layer 0.983 to 0.740. Qwen: last layer 0.99 to 0.86. Drift is concentrated in mid-depth FFN and Mamba blocks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-level (logit) matching does not preserve internal representational similarity between a compressed student and its teacher; matched outputs can coexist with divergent internal geometry.

record.problems: Only two model families are studied, and comparisons are between quantized students and their BF16 teachers rather than independently trained models. The CKA results use one similarity measure; no alternative metric, input-distribution robustness, or uncertainty estimates are reported. Several layerwise results are described qualitatively without numerical values.

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models across scale or capability.
No vision–language or paired image–caption data.
No mapping, stitching or relative representations between distinct models.
No interpretable features or circuits compared across models.
Only linear CKA on one input mixture; no metric or distribution comparison.
No independently trained models; no test of plateau or of the causes of convergence.

record.verdict_notes: All comparisons are between a model and its own quantized copy. The CKA-QAD rows reflect a CKA-maximising training loss, so they are method performance rather than evidence about convergence. No uncertainty estimates are given, and Figure 1 layer values are not tabulated.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare model sizes or capabilities, or independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
No paired image-caption data or vision-language model comparison.
No comparison across random initializations or measurement of shared features or subspaces across seeds.
CKA is used to measure and train for teacher–student geometric alignment, but the study does not test mapping, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are examined.
Uses linear CKA; does not compare similarity metrics, CKA settings such as neighbour counts, or input distributions including out-of-distribution data.

Tests how quantization and distillation objectives affect teacher–student CKA, not whether independently trained models converge naturally, plateau with scale, or converge because of shared data rather than a common model of reality.

tranche.reason: Uses CKA-guided alignment for quantization recovery and evaluates its own method; teacher-copy fidelity and induced alignment do not test the listed convergence versions.

source_check.notes: All listed values, baselines and conditions match the text. CKA-QAD rows describe induced alignment; the remaining rows measure teacher-copy fidelity, so no claim-version verdict applies.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: NVFP4 PTQ and KL-only QAD teacher–student comparisons
reader_labels.reason: Measured similarity depends on the training condition: KL-only QAD lowers CKA relative to PTQ, especially at the last layer of Nemotron and Qwen; see r1–r4 and r9–r12. These are quantized students compared with their BF16 teachers, not independently trained models.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Explicit CKA regularization restores reported similarity close to the BF16 reference, so the results show that alignment is highly dependent on the training objective rather than invariably remaining far from complete; see r5, r6, r8, r13, and r14. This is deliberately induced alignment, not evidence of spontaneous convergence.
